title: Keystore failover & HealthWatch Terraform adapter for private KMS/HSM sync
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Problem statement:
Customers running Redwood Private in VPC/on-prem have reported two operational pain points with hardware-backed keystores: 1) silent failovers when a Cloud HSM node or controller becomes unavailable leading to transient secrets errors, and 2) a lack of lightweight, platform-native health signals for keystore availability, causing long detection and recovery windows.

Goal:
Deliver a Terraform-adaptable module and small runtime operator suite (HealthWatch) that together provide: (a) deterministic failover wiring between primary KMS/HSM provider and a hot-standby vault-backed keystore, (b) drift detection for keystore connection configs and key ACLs, and (c) a battery of health probes and Prometheus-friendly metrics + PagerDuty alerts suitable for Private/VPC installs. The implementation must be fully declarative via Terraform inputs and compatible with Redwood Private's upgrade path.

Scope & deliverables:
- Terraform module: inputs for primary_hsm_provider, fallback_vault_address, keystore_role_aliases, kms_key_aliases, state_locking (S3/GCS), and optional healthwatch_lambda_config. Outputs include: keystore_endpoint, kms_connection_secret_arn, iam_role_bindings, and terraform-managed kube secret manifest.
- HealthWatch operator (small Go binary / Lambda): periodic probes for HSM control plane (RPC/TLS), Vault token reachability, latency histograms for Sign/Decrypt ops, and a lightweight keystore-failover orchestrator that can flip the application secret to fallback keystore after configurable error budget.
- Terraform test harness & examples: a reproducible terratest scenario (local HSM mock + Vault dev server) and a full deploy example for VPC-private stacks.
- Upgrade strategy: non-disruptive by default. Module exposes opt-in fields to perform a staged cutover; supports canary rollout via Redwood Console rollout policies (documented).
- Observability + alerts: Prometheus exporter metrics (keystore_up, median_sign_latency_ms, failover_count_total), Grafana dashboard JSON, and recommended alerting rules for >5% error rate over 5m or sustained median_sign_latency_ms > 250ms.
- Security & compliance: KMS/HSM private keys never leave HSM; Vault fallback uses wrapped keys and strict RBAC. Module integrates with customer KMS (Cloud KMS or onprem HSM) and supports HSM attestation during provisioning.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Terraform module deploys into an example Private cluster and produces documented outputs with no manual post-deploy steps.
2) Simulated HSM controller failure triggers HealthWatch to mark primary unhealthy and flipapp secret to fallback within configured error budget during tests.
3) All new metrics ingested into our prod-staging Prometheus; dashboard shows expected behavior.
4) Security review complete and KMS/HSM integration documented for SOC2 auditors.

Implementation notes and trade-offs:
- We will prefer a push-based failover orchestrator (HealthWatch) with opt-in automated flip to avoid unexpected cutovers for customers who want manual intervention. The Terraform module will include both automated and manual cutover wiring options.
- To avoid complex statefulness in Terraform, the module will emit a Kubernetes secret manifest and a small controller (container) will own runtime flip logic; Terraform only manages configuration and RBAC.
- For on-prem HSMs behind NAT, we’ll provide a bridge/proxy pattern that HealthWatch can run in the customer VPC as a sidecar.

Docs & artifacts:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Keystore+Failover+and+HealthWatch
- Example TF module RFC: https://docs.redwood.ai/terraform/modules/keystore-failover-rfc.md
- PR for initial module scaffolding: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/12456
- Terratest harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/tree/main/terratest/keystore-failover
